messages.text: This is a live demo of Agent Swarm. Everything here is a mock Slack workspace for a fictional company, Northwind Labs. The people are made up. The swarm is real: it runs on a small server, reads these channels, and replies in threads. Watch #ask-the-swarm.
Morning all. Board update goes out Friday, so please keep #ops and #sales current this week.
2.14 shipped: new invoice export, faster search index, fixed the timezone bug in reminders. Next up is the webhook retry queue.
Reminder that the staging database resets every Sunday night.
Pipeline this week: 14 open deals, 3 in legal review, 2 waiting on security questionnaires.
Acme asked for a comparison sheet against Contoso. I will draft one.
Ticket volume is up 20% since 2.14. Most are questions about the new export.
Three new hires start next Monday. Laptops ordered, accounts pending.
Team, this channel is for the swarm. Mention it with a request and it takes it from there.

prompts.text: <@bot> write a short FAQ entry for customers asking how the new invoice export works. Three questions, plain language.

<@bot> review this function and list any bugs:
```
function retryDelayMs(attempt) {
  const base = 200;
  return Math.min(base * 2 ** attempt, 30000) + Math.random() * 100;
}
```
<@bot> draft a two-paragraph follow-up email to a prospect who went quiet after a demo two weeks ago. Friendly, no pressure.
<@bot> turn these notes into a checklist for onboarding a new engineer: laptop, GitHub org, staging access, 1:1 with lead, read the runbook, first PR in week one.
<@bot> summarize what changed in release 2.14 for the board update. Two sentences, non-technical.
<@bot> write a SQL query that lists customers with more than 3 support tickets in the last 30 days. Tables: customers(id, name), tickets(id, customer_id, created_at).
<@bot> a customer says reminders fire one hour late since the update. Give me three questions to ask them before I escalate.
<@bot> we have 14 open deals and a target of 40 new accounts this quarter. Suggest a simple weekly tracking format for the sales channel.
<@bot> propose a rollout plan for the webhook retry queue: staging first, then 10% of customers, then everyone. Include what to watch at each step.
<@bot> give me a five-line status update for the company all-hands based on what you can see in this workspace.
<@bot> explain the difference between an exponential backoff and a fixed retry interval to a junior engineer, in five sentences.
<@bot> draft release notes for customers about the faster search index. Keep it under 80 words.
